items.title: CCPA imposes ₹1 lakh penalty on Shangri-La Eros for levying service charge on restaurant bills
items.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹1 lakh on Shangri-La Eros hotel in New Delhi for levying service charges on restaurant bills despite the Delhi High Court ruling that such charges must be voluntary. A coram comprising Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Anupam Mishra held that adding default service charges to bills and putting the burden on customers to request removal of such charges violate consumer rights and amount to unfair trade practice. The CCPA observed that merely describing a charge as optional did not make its collection voluntary when the amount was automatically included in the bill. " Merely displaying the collection of non-statutory charge like 'service charge', on the menu card or on the bill does not cure the underlying compulsion ," the Authority said. The October 22 order arose from consumer complaints received in May and June 2025 alleging that Mister Chai, a restaurant at Shangri-La Eros, had imposed a 10 percent service charge on food bills. items.title: Israeli election: why nobody has been talking about Palestinian statehood
items.summary: As Israelis head to the polls on October 27 one major issue that has not received serious attention during the campaign is Israel’s flat rejection of Palestinian statehood. This puts Israel seriously at odds with world opinion. As it stands, 159 countries around the world recognise Palestinian statehood , including diplomatic heavyweights such as the UK and France . The two UN security council members joined Australia, Andorra, Canada, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, Portugal and San Marino in formally recognising the state of Palestine in September 2025. This represents an important shift within the world’s most important diplomatic frameworks. Now, nearly half of the G7 and four of the five permanent members of the UN security council – China, France, Russia and the UK – recognise Palestine as a legitimate state. This international pressure was recently ramped up by international sanctions by the UK and others against Israeli settler groups. Given this pressure – as well as the ongoing conflict in Gaza – you’d expect opposition parties, at least, to engage with the record of the Netanyahu government on the Palestinian question. items.title: Palestinian citizens face a painful choice in Israel’s election: To vote or not
items.summary: Elections are typically framed as a choice for voters. For Palestinian citizens of Israel, however, the country’s national ballots pose more of a dilemma. Constituting about one-sixth of eligible voters in Israel, Palestinian citizens could hold the difference in a race expected to be close . But voting involves a trade-off: By casting a ballot for their best interests, many Palestinian citizens believe they also risk legitimizing a process that seeks to silence their voice and a system that treats their citizenship as conditional . The coming Israeli election on Oct. 27, 2026 , brings that tension to a new peak. Since the last general election in 2022 , the destruction and mass killing in Gaza , restrictions on Palestinian citizens’ speech and protest and leading opposition parties’ rejection of having Arab political partners have sharpened the dilemma of seeking protection through institutions that reinforce their exclusion. Having devoted most of my academic career to studying relations between Israel and its Palestinian citizens , I see the question facing Palestinian citizens of Israel as part of a much longer struggle over survival, citizenship and political belonging. items.title: Master of roster system destroying accountability of judicial system: Kapil Sibal
items.summary: Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal on Tuesday launched a critique of the administrative functioning of the higher judiciary, warning that the "master of the roster" system, backroom bargaining within the Collegium and complete opacity surrounding in-house disciplinary inquiries against judges accused of misbehaviour have triggered a crisis of public confidence. Sibal was speaking at a discussion organised by the Campaign for Judicial Accountability and Reforms (CJAR) at the India International Centre in New Delhi. He observed that while judicial pronouncements are publicly debated, the unreviewable administrative discretion of Chief Justices has left the judicial institution vulnerable to systemic erosion. "There is a public debate on the judicial side of judgments of the court. But there can't be a debate within the public on decisions which are administrative. I can't criticise a judge for fixing a matter, or Chief Justice for fixing a matter before another judge," he said. He went on to note that ultimately, a judge is only answerable to his own conscience in such matters. " How do we get accountability into the system? items.title: Supreme Court too Chief Justice-centric, encourages ‘hero worship’: Former Justice AS Oka
items.summary: Hero worship of the Chief Justice of India stems from the concentration of too much power in the office, said former Supreme Court judge Justice Abhay S Oka on Tuesday. Justice Oka made the observation in a keynote address he gave at a seminar on “Accountability of Judges” organised by the Campaign for Judicial Accountability and Reforms (CJAR). "Look at the Supreme Court... most of the administrative decisions are taken by only the Chief Justice of India. And so Chief Justice controls most of the administrative functions of the Supreme Court... because of this, all powerful position of the Chief Justice, sometimes stakeholders indulge in hero worship of Chief Justice of India," said Justice Oka. He said that such a concentration of power was a concern that had also been raised by Dr BR Ambedkar during the Constituent Assembly debates. "He (Dr BR Ambedkar) had warned all of us about serious consequence of hero worship. Because hero worship comes from absolute power concentrated in the hands of the Chief Justice of India," noted Justice Oka. items.title: In opting for Lula, Brazil made a conservative choice to elect a man of the left over one of the far right
items.summary: The 2026 elections in Brazil played out amid an widespread assumption repeated around the world : that the country was polarized and that would inform the vote. But the word “polarization” implies symmetry – and symmetry is something that never existed in the contest between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. On one side, a moderate center-left politician with a center-right running mate, Geraldo Alckmin. On the other, a representative of the radical right and a member of an international movement that critics say threatens democracies around the world. Flávio is no mere conservative. While he may be courted and supported by the members of the Republican Party in the U.S., his policies put him more in the mold of Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany and Portugal’s Enough, a party that advocates the repatriation of immigrants and a ban on Muslim places of worship. On the day he launched his candidacy, at an event of Brazil’s Liberal Party (PL) in São Paulo, Flávio laid out three of the guiding principles of what his administration would look like.
